text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.76% today after a two-week slide of 8.4%, driven primarily by weakness in crude oil prices. Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th—the first time since August—as President Trump signaled the Iran conflict may be ending soon, reducing geopolitical risk premiums that had been supporting energy prices. With Brent now at $107 and US oil at $99.64, the company faces lower revenues per barrel of oil produced, which directly pressures earnings for integrated oil producers.

The selloff has accelerated since ConocoPhillips reported third-quarter results on November 5th, suggesting the market's focus shifted from company-specific performance to the broader oil price decline. De-escalation hopes in the Middle East remove a key prop that had been supporting oil prices higher, and that structural shift affects the entire energy sector regardless of individual company execution.
